tasks.title: Build regenerator agent spawner
tasks.description:
TDD. Create and export an async function `spawnRegenerator()` in src/commands/plan.ts that spawns a non-interactive `claude -p` process to fix tasks based on review feedback. Same spawn pattern as spawnReviewer (task 5).

Signature: `spawnRegenerator(opts: { projectRoot: string, dataDir: string, projectName: string, agents: AgentInfo[], gitStatus: string, reviewFeedback: string, streamOpts?: ProcessStreamOptions, deps?: { spawn?, processStreamFn? } }): Promise<{ exitCode: number }>`

Implementation:
- Build args: `['-p', '--append-system-prompt', buildRegeneratorPrompt({...}), '--allowedTools', 'Read,Glob,Grep,Write,Edit', '--output-format', 'stream-json', '--model', 'sonnet', '--verbose']`
- User prompt: `'Read the review feedback in .ralph/review-feedback.md and fix the identified issues in .ralph/tasks.json. Preserve any completed tasks.'`
- Same spawn/stream pattern as reviewer
- Return exit code

Write tests with mocked spawn/processStream verifying correct args, allowed tools include Write+Edit, correct prompt.
tasks.notes: Implemented spawnRegenerator() following same pattern as spawnReviewer(). Key differences: allowedTools includes Write,Edit (not just Read,Glob,Grep), uses buildRegeneratorPrompt with full project context and reviewFeedback, user prompt instructs agent to fix tasks.json while preserving completed tasks. 15 tests added covering all args, stdin prompt, processStream, cwd, env, exit codes, streamOpts passthrough, and reviewFeedback inclusion in prompt. 669 total tests pass.

tasks.title: Build review loop orchestrator
tasks.description:
TDD. Create and export an async function `runAutoReview()` in src/commands/plan.ts that orchestrates the review/regeneration loop.

Signature: `runAutoReview(opts: { projectRoot: string, dataDir: string, projectName: string, agents: AgentInfo[], gitStatus: string, maxIterations: number, streamOpts?: ProcessStreamOptions, deps?: { spawnReviewerFn?, spawnRegeneratorFn?, readFileFn?, consoleLogFn? } }): Promise<ReviewResult>`

Loop logic:
1. For pass = 1 to maxIterations:
   a. Print `Auto-review pass {pass} of {maxIterations}...`
   b. Call spawnReviewer with passNumber=pass
   c. Read .ralph/review-feedback.md
   d. Parse with parseReviewFeedback()
   e. Display each dimension's score and issues (colored: green=PASS, yellow=WARN, red=FAIL)
   f. If verdict is PASS, print 'All dimensions passed. Tasks are ready for review.' and return result
   g. If not last iteration: print 'Regenerating tasks with reviewer feedback...', call spawnRegenerator with the feedback content
2. If loop exhausted without PASS: print remaining concerns from last feedback, return last result

Write tests covering: single-pass PASS (early exit), convergence on pass 2, max iterations reached with NEEDS_WORK, dimension display output.

tasks.title: Add auto-review menu option to reviewTasksLoop
tasks.description:
TDD. Add an `[a]uto-review` menu option to the `reviewTasksLoop()` function in src/commands/plan.ts. Insert it between the existing `[v]iew` and `[p]lan` options (around line 660).

The handler should:
1. Check that tasks.json exists (print error and return {exit: false} if not)
2. Load config to get review.maxIterations (default 3)
3. Call runAutoReview() with appropriate opts
4. After the loop completes, display the final review-feedback.md content if verdict is NEEDS_WORK
5. Return {exit: false} to stay in the menu loop

Update the ReviewTasksLoopOpts interface to include any new dependencies needed (projectRoot, projectName, agents, gitStatus, config). Thread these through from the caller in the plan command handler (around line 776).

Write tests verifying: menu option appears with key 'a', handler checks for tasks.json existence, handler calls runAutoReview, returns to menu after completion.

tasks.title: Make task generation auto-start
tasks.description:
Update the user prompt string on line 411 of src/commands/plan.ts in the `launchTaskGeneration()` function. Change from:

`'Read planning-notes.md and generate the task breakdown. Show me the proposed tasks for approval before writing tasks.json.'`

To something more directive like:

`'Read planning-notes.md now and generate the complete task breakdown. Present the tasks in a table, then ask if you should write tasks.json.'`

The key change is making it unambiguous that the agent should start immediately without waiting for additional human input. Write a test verifying the prompt string contains directive language (e.g., 'now', 'generate the complete').
